text:
maya: Quick sync — I want to propose a guarded rollout for the new route-by-latency config. Goal: prefer low-latency replicas but avoid oscillation during spikes. Thinking staged percentages + a telemetry gate that checks error-rate and p50 change. Thoughts?

sam: +1 on telemetry gate. Can we make it a dry-run for 24h first so we can inspect routing diffs? :eyes:

felix: Dry-run is good. Also we need a safe-fallback to route-by-cost if latency SLOs degrade beyond threshold. Otherwise we might blast expensive GPUs.

maya: Agreed. Draft plan: 1) Dry-run for 24h, 2) Canary 5% traffic with smart backoff, 3) 25% after telemetry gate, 4) 100% w/monitoring. Gate rules: p50 latency <= baseline*1.15 AND error-rate delta < 0.2%.

lee: One API note — current runtime-config schema doesn't support multi-metric gates. We'd need to extend it to include an array of checks. Minimal example: ```{"gate_checks": [{"metric":"p50_latency","op":"<=","value":1.15},{"metric":"error_rate_delta","op":"<","value":0.002}]}```

anya: Console UX: we need to surface the gate evaluation window and recent samples. Ops will want a quick "override" button for emergency pause, but it must be audited. Can we add a lightweight modal showing last 1h of metrics and a single-click pause? :warning:

console-ui-bot: Noted — I can add a prototype. Question: do we show raw metric series or just pass/fail + trend?

maya: Show pass/fail + sparkline + link to detailed dashboard. Override must require a reason and 2FA. Audit log entry recorded to config change log.

sam: Implementation details for runtime: do we evaluate gates centrally in control plane or push to the edge? Central simplifies telemetry but adds latency to decisions. Edge reduces control-plane load but needs consistent metric view.

felix: Suggest hybrid: control plane evaluates gates for rollout decisions; edge should keep a local fail-closed behavior: if it loses control plane heartbeat for >30s, revert to route-by-cost (safe default).

reliability: Also think about quota interactions. If route-by-latency sends more traffic to a pool with tight quotas, we need backpressure signals. Add quota headroom check to gate or a separate runtime guard.

maya: Good call. Add quota headroom metric (available_tokens_pct > 20%) to gate list. Also include a surge-protection thin circuit-breaker: if any backend reports 5xx rate > 1% for >1m, throttle canary to 0.

lee: I'll draft the schema change and a migration plan. Two questions: 1) back-compat — unknown gate fields should be ignored, 2) how to test in unit/e2e?

maya: For back-compat treat unknown checks as no-op. Testing: unit tests for gate parser + a simulated traffic harness for e2e in staging. ops-bot: scheduled a 24h dry-run kick at 2026-04-02T09:00Z (sim).

ops-bot: DRY-RUN TASK CREATED: route-by-latency dry-run -> start=2026-04-02T09:00Z duration=24h owner=@maya.

anya: UX request: on dry-run we should highlight "impact estimation" — show which customer segments would be affected if we flipped it live (top 10 by request volume).

sam: One more: throttling policy for override. If an engineer hits pause, console should optionally auto-escalate to paging if pause persists >10m and pass/fail status still failing.

felix: Agree. Automation: if gate fails 3x in a row during canary, auto-rollback and open incident draft.

maya: Thanks all. Next steps: lee sends schema PR, console-ui-bot puts up prototype for the modal, ops-bot will run dry-run, reliability to add quota check to telemetry dashboard. We'll reconvene after 24h dry-run to inspect diffs. :thumbsup:

reliability: Noted. I'll also add a synthetic spike test to make sure fallback behaves as expected.
